chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'When we enter Makkah and Al-Medina, do we complete (the prayer) or shorten (it)?' He said, 'If you shorten, that is it; and if you complete, it is better and increases (in reward).'
ai.seo_question: Should Muslims shorten or complete their prayers when visiting Makkah and Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic preference for performing complete (Tamm) prayers in the two holy sanctuaries, contrasting with the general rule of shortening (Qasr) during travel. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms that while shortening remains valid, completing the prayer is superior (khayr) and increases spiritual reward, reflecting the unique status of these cities as places of permanent devotion rather than mere transit points.
